Made a rep rap i2 prusia mendel a couple years back. Learned: A) that thermistors (the thingies that measure temperature on the heatbed and extruder) are super fragile and will break if you manhandle the wires. B) those thingamabobs are in toasters, and can be liberated easily. C) That making a printer was less complicated than building an ikea couch. Think lego or kinex and add the stress of having really fragile parts that are inconvenient to replace.

Bought a Prusa Mendel i2 from a shady vendor and I must say that my mileage varies.

It was quite hellish to calibrate, and some parts broke during the assembly and some others (extruder) were too low quality and had to replace them. The instructions were close to non existent. However, there were a lot of resources about Prusa Mendel i2, so I could ultimately finish it.

In my personal experience, I will trade it for any Ikea build. I know that this is my personal (and bad) experience, but I thought that I could share it.

I designed and assembled a 3d printer. Went for CoreXY because the structure does not twist and you have only one moving motor if you go for a direct extruder. Here are some things I learned

  • H7 Steel Rods no less than 10mm diameter

  • If you go for bearings don't buy cheap shitty bearings.

  • PTFE, PLA, igus bushings are better. They are quiet and don't ruin your rods

  • Enclosed printer is needed for ABS, because it curls on itself if there is no heating.

  • ABS is easier to sand and finish than PLA

  • You'll get injured. Be prepared for burns, cuts, bumps

We have 5 of them at work, from the i2 we originally got to the latest that was invented in house with a printing area of 1000x1000x1500mm

Buy quality components, you'll thank yourself later, especially when it comes to motors or bearings like /user/abruski said. Otherwise, be prepared for things not to work as expected the first time, and then the second as well. Otherwise, depending on the model you choose, it can be rather simple/quite complicated.

Also, if you want to make a reprap, and have a friend with a 3D printer, you might want to ask him to print you the plastic pieces and then buy the rest of the kit yourself, for a 3rd of the price most resellers ask.
